![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14044310/assets/ef7114aaf0f2cc275b79fe312ac6e99bda2bf07667eaa4ccfaae3920538381b5.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slope field is zero along the lines $x=0$ and $x=1.$ Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on both of these lines.

Of the given equations, the only two that satisfy this condition are

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =2{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3}=2{x}^{2}(1-x),\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+x=x(x-1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the lines $x=0$ and $x=1$ divide the plane into $3$ regions. The sign of the slopes in each of the $3$ regions is easily deduced by considering the behavior of the solution curves in these regions. This information is summarized in the following table:

| Region | $x<0$ | $0<x<1$ | $x>1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Slope | $↗$ | $↗$ | $↘$ |
| Sign | $+$ | $+$ | $-$ |

Of the two remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}=2{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3}.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is ${y}^{′}=2{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3}.$
